summary:
# NOTES: *In the Days of Drake* (J. S. Fletcher, 1897; Gutenberg #29304)

Single book, no BOOK divisions. Narrator: Humphrey Salkeld, an old man writing memoir of 1578–1580.

## Preface (unsigned intro, signed J. S. Fletcher)
- Praises Elizabethan age: Drake, Frobisher, Hawkins, Raleigh, Grenville, Gilbert; "sea-dogs."
- Spain = "retrogressive force," black cruelties; Armada beaten. "God's will that not Spain but England should win."

## Ch I: Home, friends, surroundings
- Narrator born York 1558. Father Richard Salkeld, attorney, youngest son of Oliver Salkeld, lord of Beechcot-on-the-Wold. Father and mother die of fever when he is six.
- Uncle Sir Thurstan Salkeld of Beechcot (knighted by Queen, magistrate, never married) adopts him as heir.
- Aunt Dame Barbara Stapleton (Thurstan's sister; widow of Devereux Stapleton, Queen's household officer) and son Jasper Stapleton (same age, orphan) move in.
- Barbara overheard: "'Tis neither right nor just..." Thurstan: "Dick's boy should step into his father's place." Will educate Jasper, leave him money.
- Narrator now magistrate and church-warden; once told story to the King at Whitehall, introduced by Sir Ralph Wood (Parliament man, neighbor).
- Vicar Rev. Timotheus Herrick (tall, thin, absent-minded scholar); wife Mistress Priscilla Horbury ("managing"). Daughter Rose, 3 yrs younger, outpaces the boys in lessons.

## Ch II: Pharaoh Nanjulian (June 1575)
- Village inn kept by Geoffrey Scales. Constable John Broad. Drawer Peter Pipe (cowardly).
- Sailor Pharaoh Nanjulian: Cornishman of Marazion, huge, black beard, blue-red tattoos on arms, gold earrings, bare callused feet.
- His story: wrecked off Norway with 16 men; Drontheim; Scarborough; walking home. Threw tankard at Peter for serving small beer. Palermo bear story.
- Village talk: Dame Good lost two fowls; two linen sheets stolen from vicarage hedge.
- Pharaoh pays a groat for Peter's jaw; Sir Thurstan fines him ten groats, orders Peter admonished (Geoffrey: "with a stick"). Gives 12 shillings; advises ship from Hull.
- Pharaoh: "Pharaoh Nanjulian never forgets."

## Ch III: Rose (spring 1578)
- Narrator (19) and Jasper both love Rose. Narrator writes poem "To Rose" ("When I first beheld thee, dear"). Jasper reads it over his shoulder.
- Lots drawn with wheat-stack straws; narrator's straw a foot longer. Jasper: "I will wait."
- Narrator proposes to Rose in vicarage garden; she: "Are you a boy again?" Betrothed.
- Jasper: "I see how it is... You have no need to speak." Vows hatred.

## Ch IV: Foul play (Oct 1578)
- Summer: Thurstan approves betrothal; wedding set for two years hence. Jasper seen with dead deer in woods.
- Rose: "He will do you a mischief... jealousy breeds murder."
- Oct 1578: Thurstan sends both to Scarborough for Hamburg ship's goods. Stay at Mermaid Tavern. Later Three Jolly Mariners inn (carved figurehead).
- Captain Manuel Nunez of Seville: tall, jet-black hair, eyes close-set, big white teeth, smile "like a dog that shows its fangs," trimmed pointed beard.
- Invites them aboard Santa Luisa, 6 o'clock. Drugged; narrator wakes in hammock after 12 hrs, off Lincolnshire coast.

## Ch V: Pharaoh again (voyage)
- Nunez lies: narrator confessed a crime, Jasper and narrator paid 200 English guineas for passage to West Indies. Narrator denies, says "Jasper... foul conspiracy."
- Destination claimed: Barbadoes or Martinique. Narrator penniless.
- ~3 weeks out, past Ushant: gale; rescue of wreck survivor, "mariner of Plymouth, sole survivor of ship Hawthorn." It is Pharaoh.

## Ch VI: Schemes
- Pharaoh coils rope, speaks low; recalls oath to serve Sir Thurstan.
- Signals: wink, nod, cough. Crew all Spanish or Portuguese; bo's'n Pedro.
- Pharaoh learns: destination Vera Cruz; Jasper bargained for narrator's death (wanted him knocked on head, thrown overboard); Nunez to hand him to Holy Office. Pharaoh saw two Englishmen burnt in Mexico City ten years earlier.
- Plan: escape by boat.

## Ch VII: We escape the Spaniards (Christmas 1578)
- Sighted Orizaba peak (~17,000 ft) Christmas morning; Tuxtla volcano.
- Nunez: "two hundred English guineas" ; "kind and considerate host."
- Narrator climbs into boat at stern; Pharaoh joins, cuts adrift.

## Ch VIII: An unknown land
- Landed on Mexican coast. Pharaoh rows all night toward Tuxtla fire. Nunez 20-35 miles off.
- Prickly pears; wild turkey; flint and steel. Two days through woods. Plain of Orizaba; steer by Virgo to Acapulco.
- Night refuge: half-ruined Indian hut.

## Ch IX: Adventure of some importance
- Day six: narrator sees black-cowled face (eye-slits) over rock. Pharaoh: "'Tis a Familiar."
- Road Oaxaca–Vera Cruz. Coach attacked by two ruffians; narrator and Pharaoh beat them off.
- Old gentleman ("Caramba!") and daughter Isabella; coachman Pedro Gomez, servants Chispa, Antonio. Gentleman gives meat, wine, purse. Pharaoh speaks Spanish, claims Catalonia.

## Ch X: The black shadows
- Mountain 3-4k ft. Sunlit rock shows shadows: cowled monk and feathered Indian; eventually twelve Indians.

## Ch XI: Captive
- Monk Frey Bartolomeo de los Rios: thin, pale, bright eyes, low sweet voice; "hunter" of heretics.
- Poisoned arrows. Pharaoh gives names: "Master Humphrey Salkeld of Yorkshire" and self, shipwrecked mariner.
- Marched to Mexico City (4th day).

## Ch XII: More cruel than wild beasts
- Entered by gate of St. Catherine; Placa del Marquese. Crowd gives food, money (noblewoman).
- Nunez mocks: "what was born to be burned will never be drowned." Narrator spits in his face (hands tied); Nunez draws rapier; monk stops him.
- Held in hospital with other Englishmen (sailors, merchants). Inquisitors absent; return Ash Wednesday 1579; separate dungeons.
- Old gentleman (Pharaoh's rescued man) promises influence with Chief Inquisitor.
- Narrator examined ~3 weeks before Easter; interpreter Robert Sweeting (half-breed). Questions: transubstantiation, Luther. Narrator says he is "simple country gentleman."
- Racked that night by Bartolomeo.

## Ch XIII: Auto-da-fe (Good Friday 1579)
- Scaffold in main square; drums and trumpets. San-benitos (yellow cotton). Halters, green candles. Viceroy present; ~300 friars.
- Sentences:
  - Thomas White, Cornelius Johnson, Peter Brown, Henry More: 300 lashes on horseback, 10 yrs galleys.
  - William Collier, Thomas Ford, John Page: 200 lashes, 8 yrs.
  - Stephen Brown, Nicholas Peterson (Dutch): 100 lashes, 6 yrs.
  - Narrator and Pharaoh: 2 yrs galleys (lightest).
  - Burned: William Moor, John Wood, Hans Schewitzer (German Lutheran).
- Lashed through streets; criers "Behold these English dogs, Lutherans."
- Nunez: "Our Holy Office is merciful... sadly too merciful for my liking."

## Ch XIV: On board the galley
- Narrator and Pharaoh put in one cell. Old gentleman visits with basket; gives names of Spanish friends (for escape).
- Marched overland to Acapulco, chained at wrist and ankle.
- Ship: treasure galleon Santa Filomena (to return via Pacific islands, Africa, avoiding Hawkins/Drake/Frobisher). Chained at oars; negro slaves on other benches.
- Pharaoh: "Heart up, master!"

## Ch XV: Nunez in a new guise
- Nunez and Bartolomeo visit. Nunez: "I will kill you by inches." Narrator: "God gives His power to men" pushback.
- Bartolomeo to a fellow prisoner: "With heretics we keep no faith. To thy oar, Lutheran!"

## Ch XVI: Flag of England
- Narrator and crew beaten daily by overseers; Nunez personally whips and tortures.
- Branded "Heretic" on back and breast; salted.
- Nunez taunts narrator about Jasper and "the lady whose affections you stole from him"; narrator weeps; "So you are broken at last," struck across mouth.
- Nine or ten weeks at sea; a sail chases them; English flag.

## Ch XVII: Francis Drake
- Galley crew cheer; Spaniards whip harder. English ship fires shot, then grapples and boards.
- Englishmen with hammers and chisels break chains. Pharaoh identifies Drake: "gold band round his scarlet cap."
- Drake: high forehead, crisp brown hair, steady gray eyes, plaited cord with ring; age 30; first circumnavigation.
- Narrator tells Drake of Nunez and Bartolomeo: "do justice upon them."

## Ch XVIII: Fate of Nunez and Frey Bartolomeo
- Second English ship arrives. Drake's order: bring both aboard unharmed.
- Nunez found in cabin; killed two Englishmen first; Pharaoh seizes him. Nunez: "'Tis fate."
- Bartolomeo in powder magazine with lit candle; threatens to blow ship. Pharaoh knocks candle away.
- Treasure: jewels, fourteen chests of ryals of plate, 100+ lb gold, 20 tons uncoined silver, plate.
- Drake: Nunez and Bartolomeo hanged from yard-arm of Santa Filomena. Spanish survivors released with warning.

## Ch XIX: Home with Drake
- Mid-August (1580), North Pacific. Ternate (5 Nov), Celebes shoal (mid-Jan, cargo jettisoned), Java (March), Cape of Good Hope (June).
- Plymouth Sound, third week Sept 1580, "two years and some ten months" voyage. Queen knights Drake on Golden Hinde.
- Drake gives narrator gold.
- Pharaoh made boatswain's mate; refuses to come home: "I am Francis Drake's man now."

## Ch XX: Beechcot once more (Oct 1580)
- Rides from Plymouth via Exeter, Bristol, Derby, Sheffield, York. Bearded, scarred, two inches taller.
- Beechcot inn: Geoffrey Scales recognizes him.
- Rose at vicarage, sewing: "Humphrey!" Jasper had told that narrator drowned at Scarborough after visiting a captain at night.
- Master Timotheus recognizes him; cries, "Rose's face was brighter."

## Ch XXI: How they rang the bells at Beechcot
- Moonlit churchyard; parents' monument now has new inscription: "Humphrey Salkeld... drowned at Scarborough, October, 1578."
- Jasper meets him in the churchyard/Duke's Garth. Jasper: "Dead men call nobody." Admits trick: "Because you stood 'twixt me and the inheritance."
- Jasper draws rapier; narrator knocks it away with cudgel, beats him, flings him against wall. Jasper and Dame Barbara vanish from Beechcot.
- Thurstan in great hall: "Is that Jasper?" "Nay, sir... It is I--Humphrey." Narrator rings great bell; village rejoices.
- Married Rose in Beechcot church within weeks; "fifty years of blessed companionship."
- ~20 years later, Pharaoh visits; lives with narrator 10 more years; dies near 100.
- End.

## Transcriber's note
- Minor typesetting corrections only.
